tweaks.name: Multimedia network throttling off
tweaks.description: Removes the MMCSS limit of about 10 packets per millisecond (roughly 100 Mbit/s with full-size packets) that Windows applies to network traffic while audio or video is playing. It does not lower ping; it can help big downloads on fast connections while sound plays, but its effect on current Windows versions is poorly measured, so it is off by default.

tweaks.name: Immediate TCP acknowledgements (Nagle/delayed ACK off)
tweaks.description: Sets TcpAckFrequency=1 (documented by Microsoft) and the legacy TCPNoDelay=1 on every current network interface so Windows acknowledges TCP data at once instead of waiting up to 200 ms. Only older TCP-based online games benefit; most modern games use UDP and are unaffected, and adapters added later are not covered.
